summary.headline: True Colors FY26 revenue rose 29.22% to INR 301.55 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.58% and PAT at INR 31.16 crore, but operating cash flow was negative.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR 301.55 crore (up 29.22% YoY), EBITDA INR 46.98 crore (15.58% margin) and PAT INR 31.16 crore (10.33% margin). Recurring revenue from ink, sublimation paper and spares was about 50.25% of revenue. Operating cash flow was negative (about INR 35 crore), which management attributed to MSME payment-term compliance, Konica Minolta advance-payment terms and a rise in receivables to INR 111 crore at March-end, now reported at about INR 93 crore. Management is moving ink from trading to in-house manufacturing under the INKIA brand, with a phased capex plan.

financial_highlights.change: Prior-year H2 margin cited as 17.5%; full-year FY25 margin cited as about 18%
Compared with a figure of about INR 31 crore in the analyst's question (sign and comparison not clarified)

financial_highlights.value: About INR 111 crore (INR 101 crore cited earlier in the call)
financial_highlights.change: Nearly doubled YoY per analyst; about INR 93 crore as of the call date
Up from 89 units in prior year; machine revenue grew over 155x YoY per management
About 19% volume growth as reported; management says underlying growth is near 20% after adding back about 45-50 tons bundled with machines

financial_highlights.value: Ink about INR 74 crore; sublimation paper about INR 65-66 crore; spares about INR 10-10.5 crore

financial_highlights.change: Up from INR 11 crore in prior-year H2; H2 revenue cited at about INR 150 crore vs INR 140 crore

segments.name: Machines / technology and consumables
segments.commentary: About 109 machines placed in FY26 across five OEM lines (Konica Minolta, Eton, Pangda, SkyJet, HopeTech); management cites a shift toward higher-value machines. Installed base is about 900+ machines. Average machine realization was INR 25-27 lakh last year, and management declined to give a current-year average.

segments.name: Ink
segments.commentary: FY26 reported ink volume was 1,140 tons, with ink revenue about INR 74 crore. Ink is being moved from import/distribution to in-house manufacturing under INKIA; INKIA produced about 80 tons per month last year and 80 tons was added via the merger.

segments.name: Sublimation paper
segments.commentary: Capacity was raised from about 1 crore to over 2 crore meters per month, with FY26 utilization at about 52%. Realization fell as average GSM dropped from 45-55 to about 35; FY26 realization was about INR 5.6 per meter; paper revenue about INR 65-66 crore.

segments.name: Printed fabric / job work and fabric supply
segments.commentary: Digital fabric printing capacity is 75,000 meters per day. Revenue split is about 50:50 between customer-supplied fabric (job work) and company-bought fabric. About 6% of fabric revenue is direct export.

segments.name: Commercial printing (new)
segments.commentary: Early-stage entry into label, mica and packaging printing, starting as a trading/distribution business with no additional capex planned. No service team has been added yet.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth guided at about 20-22% a year, with profitability growth expected to outpace the top line.
EBITDA margin: management says the 14-16% range is sustainable near term, with improvement over time from in-house ink and paper; it did not commit to a return to 18%.
Ink Phase-1 targets 150 tons per month in-house capacity in FY27 at capex of INR 40-45 crore, with production to start by end-2026 and realization in FY27.

Ink Phase-2 targets 500 tons per month in FY28 with additional capex of INR 20-25 crore; Phase-3 targets 1,000 tons per month over three to four years with land about 3.5 times the existing footprint.
Capex funding: about 25% from internal accruals and 75% from bank debt. Working capital bank limit is INR 40 crore.
capex_capacity: Sublimation paper capacity expanded to over 2 crore meters per month; FY26 utilization about 52%, with headroom to grow without further capital deployment.
Digital fabric printing capacity at 75,000 meters per day.
Ink Phase-1: 150 tons/month, capex INR 40-45 crore, FY27 target; INKIA merger adds 80 tons/month; 270 tons/month to be added incrementally.
Ink Phase-2: 500 tons/month by FY28, additional capex INR 20-25 crore. Phase-3: 1,000 tons/month longer term.
INKIA merger is awaiting NCLT approval after BSE approval. Self-consumption is about 100 tons this year, rising to about 110-115 tons per month on average from next year.
demand_pricing: Management says India's digital printing share is about 7-8% versus about 85-90% in Europe and 40-50% in China; India imports about 12,000 tons of digital textile ink per month.
Ink realization assumed at INR 200-300 per liter for the planned capacity, with the mix including sublimation, reactive, pigment, solvent and UV inks.
Sublimation paper realization fell as GSM dropped; management says margin held because raw material cost fell in step.
Machine price range is INR 15-50 lakh for entry-level models and INR 60 lakh to INR 13 crore for reactive printers.
Management says rotary printing in India is about 2,400-2,600 crore meters annually and that new capacity is skewing toward digital (about 80:20 for new capacity).

qa_highlights.question: What is normalized cash conversion, and are receivables a quality issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the receivables build to MSME compliance and said there is no customer-specific issue; receivables fell from INR 111 crore at March-end to about INR 93 crore by the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter commercial printing (labels, mica, packaging)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company says the same ink formulation capability can serve commercial printers; it is a first step via trading, with aggressive expansion only if market feedback is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 18% last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix effect: paper revenue was concentrated in H2 last year, and about 45-50 tons of ink bundled with machines this year was not reported as ink revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INKIA ink be accepted by customers versus imported ink?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INKIA has supplied about 2-2.5 years, with 2,000-2,500 tons of white-label ink consumed, and that compatibility testing is a 4-5 year journey that is already complete.

qa_highlights.question: How is the ink capex funded and what working capital days are targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is 25% internal accruals and 75% bank debt; the working capital limit is INR 40 crore. Management did not give a working-capital days target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the machine revenue per unit and the ink revenue from bundling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machine realization varies widely by model and declined to give a current average; the bundled ink revenue is expected to show up in future ink revenue.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in FY26 and working-capital stretch from MSME 45-day payment compliance and Konica Minolta advance-payment terms.
Receivables of about INR 111 crore at March-end; about INR 93 crore recovered by call date; general terms are 90-120 days.
Ink Phase-1 is targeted to begin production by year-end and to earn realization in FY27; execution and customer acceptance of INKIA ink remain open.
Realization pressure in sublimation paper as GSM falls, and the EBITDA margin band of 14-16% is management's stated range.
Bank debt funding of about 75% of ink capex, and the INKIA merger's NCLT approval is pending.
Management declined to split margins by division or give a return on the ink capex.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term ecosystem and capacity plans, but cautious and sometimes evasive on near-term numbers: it declined to give machine realization, segment margins, working-capital days and a revenue CAGR figure, and repeated the 14-16% margin range.
key_quotes: So, we expect to grow at around 20% to 22% over the medium term and profitability growth should outpace the top line.
But I am pleased to share that collections have been strong in Q1 FY27 and the position has normalized now.
Our installation base today stand at around 900 plus machines and roughly 50% of our FY26 revenue is recurring.

adds.what: Ink Phase-3, 1,000 tons/month (3-4 years, land ~3.5x existing footprint)

growth.why: Management guides 20-22% medium-term revenue CAGR (midpoint 21%) with profitability growing faster; backing is partly specific (Ink Phase-1 150 t/month at INR 40-45 cr targeted for FY27, 52% sublimation paper utilisation with headroom) but the medium-term growth target itself lacks order or contract support.
